name: DE at-large
label: Safe D

key_factors: Delaware's 8-point Democratic lean plus a strong national environment for the party
Incumbent Sarah McBride has a massive financial edge ($5.1M raised, $2.7M on hand)
Republican Joseph Arminio has raised only about $6,600 with no outside support
Prediction markets price McBride at roughly 99% to win
model.rationale: Every fundamental points the same way: a Democratic-leaning state, an incumbent with overwhelming fundraising superiority, and a challenger with essentially no resources. Markets price this at near-certain Democratic victory, consistent with a low-20s expected margin.
model.watch: A late, well-funded outside intervention on the Republican side is the only plausible path to making this competitive, and nothing currently signals one.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Delaware's at-large House seat sits in a state that leans Democratic by about eight points, and first-term incumbent Sarah McBride is seeking reelection with a dominant financial position. She has raised over $5 million and holds $2.7 million on hand, with modest outside support and no recorded opposition spending. Republican challenger Joseph Arminio has raised under $7,000 and has no outside backing, leaving him with minimal means to communicate with voters.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets price McBride's chances at roughly 99 percent. With the incumbent advantage, the state's partisan lean, and a favorable national environment all aligned, the race is rated Safe Democratic with an expected margin in the low twenties.
